newsitem.title: CANADA: "En francais" only, Quebec audience tells Aznavour.
newsitem.headline: "En francais" only, Quebec audience tells Aznavour.

text.p: French singer Charles Aznavour became an unwitting victim of Quebec's endless language wars when audiences chastised him for singing some songs in English at concerts in Montreal and Ottawa.
Several members of the audience at Montreal's Molson Centre chanted "En francais, en francais" on Friday as the 72-year-old crooner offered part of his repertoire in English.

Aznavour, who has a greatest hits album in English, was annoyed by the outburst, said Bill Brownstein, arts columnist for The Gazette, Montreal's English-language daily newspaper. He faced a similar backlash when he sang in English at the National Arts Centre on Monday in Ottawa, Canada's bilingual capital in the province of Ontario.
Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien, who attended the Ottawa concert, was so upset by the audience behaviour that he apologised to Aznavour backstage.
Concert promoters said about 20 percent of the crowd at the Montreal concert was English speaking. At his second show in Montreal on Saturday, Aznavour did not sing or speak in English.

About 80 percent of Quebec's 7.1 million residents are French-speaking. After a divisive referendum on independence that separatists narrowly lost in October 1995, language is again at the centre of the battle for the hearts and minds of the province's voters.
Aznavour has always been hugely popular in Montreal, a city where many foreign performers, including British singers and rock bands, made their North American breakthroughs.
Born of Armenian parents in Paris, he reportedly quipped that the next time he performs in Montreal he might sing only in Armenian.
